summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.21/3909)

data.turoyo: Kulle səryoye wayye, kulle. Mu taʕadda d səmme aʕlayye, taʕaddat ġalabe, haw qadiri d mtaḥməli, ǧbiri hawən ṭaye".
data.translation: They were all Syriacs, all of them. From the oppression that they inflicted upon them, much oppression, they were not able to endure; they were forced to become Muslims.”

rationale: Thin active Infectum after one inherited context: human community rather than jealousy as experiencer, with oppression recoverable from the preceding clause. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (Jan 4.I/433)

data.turoyo: Ono mu ʕamano no, bas! W gdomarno w gədmʔakadno i žġaliyaṯe. W ono kmətḥamalno u mede d komarno w tawdi!
data.translation: I am of this people, that is all! And I will say it and I will affirm that statement. And I bear responsibility for what I say, and thank you!

rationale: First active I.2 example; statement and affirmation provide the context for responsibility without relying on an isolated English gloss. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: Restore š in fayəš
rationale: The corpus at 2/55 reads Bas haw fayəš mitaḥmilowa. The glossary’s fayəs substitutes s for š. Other glossary occurrences consistently attest fayəš; this is not an accent or clitic change.

summary: All seven occurrences reviewed. Active1 includes tolerance of people, reciprocal ḥḏoḏe and suffering; emotional nouns stand as zero-marked experiencer subjects. No new active sense is established.

Active mtaḥm- has l-series Preterit agents, with pronominal or reciprocal patients; lexical initial t does not identify Detransitive. Detransitive mitaḥm- makes the burden the subject/topic and leaves the experiencer generic.

Detransitive 20/7 expresses inability to endure heat under negation; inherited2/55 has the same evaluative function in Infectum-wa. The new explicit Detransitive gloss describes existing boxes, not a newly discovered paradigm.

Allowed lookup confirms ḥml III also has both heat/unbearability examples. This competing analysis remains editorially unresolved; the active paradigm supports retaining the assigned tḥml entry pending reconciliation.
The Farida reciprocal example and Talay1/140 (LB140) are inherited and not duplicated. Source spelling differences such as xŭdi+hno are not normalized into the inherited text.
Round 2 only. Jan English is a project machine translation; semantic decisions are based on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals remain prior material and are not re-proposed here.
Jan 2.21/3909 continues active tolerance with human experiencers and no overt object in the complement. This supports the round-1 participant account.
Lexical t in tḥml does not itself mark Detransitive. kmətḥamalno plus direct content object is active; no Jan Detransitive example or new Detransitive sense is proposed.
Permitted ḥml lookup confirms mḥamele/maḥmele and the duplicated heat Detransitive noted in round 1. It does not establish the s-bearing məstaḥmelan; no inherited correction is repeated.

The responsibility use could be a contact-associated extension in public speech, but this corpus alone cannot establish source language or direction of borrowing. No independent light-verb collocation is present.
Should ḥml III and tḥml I share these Detransitive forms, or should the two inherited attributions be reconciled?
Confirm segmentation of lo+mṫaḥmàllallan, especially plural experiencer and first-plural patient endings.
Is there a productive distribution between human and personified-emotion subjects, or only lexical freedom? Evidence here does not settle that distinction.
Is məstaḥmelan (Jan 2.4/807) a tḥml variant, separate stḥml loan pattern, or a transcription issue? Preserve the spelling until confirmed.
Confirm I.2 responsibility as a conventional extension of tḥml rather than a single rhetorical coercion; only Jan 4.I/433 supports it here.
Active experiencer can be a human group, conscience or passion/jealousy. Emotion subject at MAC Dawid/15 repeats a participant type already present in inherited active boxes.
